finally did a skincare routine 🦦💗 this is just what i use and it might not work for everyone! i found the best way to treat my acne and other skin issues was learning more about my skin (my skin type, what kind of acne with my dermatologist) and my biggest piece of advice for anyone who is dealing with skin issues: it’s not permanent and things take time! a pimple can take 1-2 weeks to form and a few more to go away and a lot of products take just as long to show results. i learned to normalize acne/skin issues because everyone goes through them and that’s helped my anxiety/stress when it comes to how my skin looks so much. i’ll probably make another video about how i desensitized myself to my skin issues and how important that is 🤍 i just started up tretinoin a month ago at 0.025% twice a week and my skin has been incredibly dry but i think i’ve finished most of the purging 🙂 excited to see more results from it! products 🪽: @mixsoon_official bean cleansing oil + centella cleansing foam @anua.skincare_us toner pads @mediheal_official tea tree toner pads @Pyunkang Yul (편강율) essence toner @imfrom_global mugwort essence @apieu.official madecassoside cream 2x tretinoin 0.025% (prescription) @Kiehl’s Since 1851 avocado eye cream @Laniege_us lip sleeping mask #skincare #skincareroutine #skincareproducts #koreanskincare #asianskincare #koreanskincareroutine #koreanskin #glassskin #acnetreatment

What I actually do for my skin — and almost none of it is topical. These are my opinions, not medical advice. Work with a doctor and find what fits you: → Clean water, to drink and to bathe in. Reverse osmosis or distilled, plus a shower filter. Your skin is in contact with it every single day. → Pay attention to your digestion. Consistent, regular bowel movements track with my skin more reliably than almost anything else I've noticed. It's daily feedback and it's free. → Go easy on high-glycemic foods. Everyone knows sugar in excess isn't doing them favors — almost nobody acts on it. → Get enough protein. Food first, and essential amino acids are the one supplement I trust. → Zinc and selenium, ideally from food — red meat covers both well. Worth knowing if you ever go the supplement route: high-dose zinc over time can interfere with copper absorption, so food sources keep that balanced for you without any thinking. → Enough fiber. Unglamorous and the one I'd put money on before anything else on this list. → Enough potassium, and I use topical magnesium. On the magnesium I'll be straight — absorption through skin is debated and I can't prove the mechanism. I just like how I feel on it. → Protect your sleep. Dark room, no screens late, consistent timing. The least interesting item here and the one I'd defend hardest. Just what works for me.
